summary: Guilin suits slower scenic travel shaped by karst landscapes, riverside movement, old-town texture, and easy day-to-evening visual transitions.
transport_notes: Keep riverfront, old-city, and hill-viewpoint stops grouped to avoid scattering the day across wider scenic areas.
Short rides plus walking usually works better than repeatedly jumping between distant mountain-view locations.
Evenings are strongest near central riverfronts and old-town food streets rather than far scenic detours.

budget_notes.low: Focus on public viewpoints, riverside walks, and central local-food streets.
budget_notes.medium: Blend one city landmark, one scenic river or hill stop, and one recognizable local dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Add slower comfort pacing, scenic dining, and more selective low-transfer routing.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Guilin should keep scenery accessible, photogenic, and easy to combine with affordable local food.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize observation, riverside pacing, and calm scenic immersion.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should center on mountain silhouettes, river breeze, and soft evening atmosphere.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should use easy city viewpoints, flatter scenic walks, and manageable movement.
